name: Sierra Leone
rule: Government addresses first: where a government body already has addresses, N-Ways uses its data and creates nothing new; N-Ways codes only where nothing official exists.
criteria: 0. Government addresses first: in Freetown City Council's area the FCC Plus Code is the address, shown exactly as FCC writes it

1. Easy to remember and effortless to get: a community or town name people already use + a short number, unique in Sierra Leone on its own (same-named areas share one national range); the app shows "Your home code" without being asked
2. Same grid as Freetown City Council: every spot code is a Plus Code; the gate's Plus Code is on every record and plate
3. No dependence on administrative boundaries (the 2017 reorganisation and the redistricting approved in 2025): areas and towns are N-Ways-frozen names and points
4. Building and door level: every compound, gate, structure, flat and shop
5. Stable: codes never move or get reused; regrouping never changes an issued code
6. Open and offline; privacy: codes describe places, never people

compound.digits: 3–5 (no leading zero): the length of the name's national range; grouped 482 / 27 16 / 172 16
compound.plate: <plate name> <grouped number> · <gate Plus Code, short, with town>; the official area name in small type
compound.uniqueness: name + number unique in Sierra Leone on its own: all areas with the same normalised name share one national range, the number falls in exactly one area's block; no town, district, comma or position needed

spot.form: Open Location Code, short form + reference town
spot.note: identical to the Plus Codes FCC uses

freetown.body: Freetown City Council (and any council later created from its area)
freetown.address: FCC Plus Code for the property, verbatim; street address where it exists
freetown.nwaysIssues: N-Ways codes beside FCC's Plus Code, which is shown first; compounds, gates, structures, profiles

coverage.others: any council found to address properties is added the same way (Bo, Kenema, Makeni, Koidu not verified)

import: FCC agreement for address fields only (Plus Code, location; property ID and footprint if FCC agrees); outside the public repo if terms require
residents: Plus Code typed from the FCC document + photo; accepted only if its cell lies on the compound footprint or within one cell
official.display: verbatim with the body name: "FCC Plus Code: FQR7+HX Freetown"; N-Ways layers beside in words; property IDs never public; unknown FCC code -> gate Plus Code labelled as a location

areas.what: named address areas, frozen at first issue, each named after a community, town or village people already use; no administrative parent
areas.never cross: the Sierra Leone River estuary (Freetown peninsula vs Lungi/Bullom shore), the Sherbro estuary and island, the Mano/Moa/Sewa/Rokel rivers where no bridge joins both banks

seeds.source: OpenStreetMap place=* nodes (Freetown communities mapped by residents and SLURC/YMCA mappers), N-Ways gazetteer, names confirmed by residents

build: assign each compound to the nearest primary place within 4 km, else the nearest secondary place within 15 km
split an area over 4,500 compounds among the neighbourhoods/hamlets inside it (Freetown wards are not used: they change)
fold an area under 20 compounds into its nearest neighbour

keep the name people use even where other areas share it (same-named areas share one national range: names); the code carries the area's plate name (names.plate), at most 12 characters and 2 words; a digit in a name is written as a word ("Koya Town 2" -> "Koya Two"), so the number is always last
areas.digits: the length of the area's name range (names.range); sized alone an area would need the smallest d ≥ 3 with 9×10^(d−1) ≥ 2 × compounds

names.rule: the remembered code (plate name + number) is unique nationally on its own: every area whose PLATE name normalises to the same key draws its numbers from one national range for that name, split into frozen blocks, one per area, with spare units for future areas of the name

steps: words folded: tong→town, kru→kroo, saint→st, mount→mt, &→and, one…ten→1…10, ii→2, iii→3
normalise.frozen: a fold added later never merges two names that already have blocks

range.block: max(1, ceil(2 × compounds / unit size)) whole units per area (half the block free for new houses)
range.order: area seeds along the national Hilbert curve, ties by area id; packed from the bottom
range.spare: at least 9 units (10%) unallocated at the top of every name's range
range.digits: smallest d in 3..5 with Σ blocks + 9 ≤ 90

names.decode: name_key(name) → name record; the number's length selects the range; the block holding the number is the one area; a number in the spare or no block is no address; never decoded by position or context
frozen: blocks never move, shrink or get renumbered
a new area with an existing name (or a full block) takes the next whole units from the name's spare
spare exhausted → the name opens an extension range of d+1 digits (own 90 units and spare); numbers of different lengths never collide
beyond 5 digits → the new area takes one of the name's listed qualifiers

qualified.rule: only for a name whose areas together do not fit in 5 digits: split once before first issue into established names people already say (a quarter or section name in use), each with its own range; listed here and never changed

names.nameId: 4 digits, national, frozen at issue (3,706 plate names)
names.officialArea: FCC's area takes blocks like every other area; FCC's Plus Code is shown first there

examples.area: Looking Town (Freetown): the same plate name, another block
officially Masorie Community (Western Area Rural); plate name Masorie
Masorie village (Tonkolili District), about 42 km away: the same plate name, another block

names.register: model/name-ranges.json (tools/name_ranges.py), frozen at issue; engine/data/register.json and registry/areas.csv carry it

plate.rule: every address area has two names: the official name (from the map or the council list, printed small on cards and plates, never required) and the plate name, the one said and typed in the code

limit.count: every character of the NFC form: letters, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes, an accented letter is one
limit.words: parts between spaces or hyphens, not counting of / the / and / on / at
limit.digits: none (the number is always last); a digit in a name is written as a word

plate.engine: engine/reference/plate_names.py (the shared rule) and sl_address.plate_name_ok / check_plate_name: the engine refuses a code or plate whose name is over the limit
plate.derivation: tools/name_ranges.py, language en (English and Krio names, with Temne, Mende, Limba ... words)
steps: spelling: ", Sierra Leone" and a leading * dropped; spaced dashes joined ("Tombo - Banka" -> "Tombo-Banka"); names typed in capitals written in title case; a bracketed Roman numeral kept as a word ("Kemedugu (II)" -> "Kemedugu II"); digits written as words ("Badasuma 2" -> "Badasuma Two")
always dropped: Community, Comm, Estate, Area, text in other brackets

Town, Village, Ville: dropped only at the end of a name that is over the limit ("Adonkia Village" -> "Adonkia"); kept wherever the name fits, because many names are said whole (Allen Town, Congo Town, Murray Town; Kissy Town is not Kissy)
if still over: the most distinctive run of whole words, dropping only landmark words (Junction, Wharf, Street, Corner, Quarry, Line, Mosque ...: "Gbangbatoke Junction" -> "Gbangbatoke")

never automatic: dropping a place word, a person's name, a qualifier (Upper, Lower, New, Old, Small) or a number; a short form that is the name of another area ("Moyamba Junction" is not Moyamba) or of a well-known town (avoid list); a short form that is not a place name alone ("Police"); these go to the council
plate.avoid: district headquarters and big towns, the 31 reference towns, every area mapped as place=town or city, and the neighbouring countries and their capitals; the area's own town (within 5 km) is allowed

known.rule: a documented short form people already say, with its source

plate.council: needsCouncilChoice areas carry up to 3 candidates and a reason; the first candidate that keeps every qualifier and is not a well-known town is used provisionally so that the area can be numbered, else the cleaned name (over the limit until the council chooses). The district or city council, with the chiefdom, confirms or chooses the plate name; the area's numbers never change
plate.aliases: the official name's key decodes to the plate name when it belongs to exactly one plate name and is no plate name itself; otherwise it is not an alias (listed in model/name-ranges.json -> plates.droppedAliases)
plate.fields: registry/areas.csv: plate_name, official_name, needs_council_choice; model/name-ranges.json: plateRule (as-is, cleaned, distinctive, known, council), plateCandidates, plateReason, plateSource

numbering.order: one Hilbert curve (order 16) over a fixed national frame [6.85, −13.35, 10.05, −10.20], by compound anchor (gate)
numbering.spacing: inside the area's block [lo, hi]: number_i = lo + i×step + step div 2, step = (hi − lo + 1) div N
numbering.later: free number halfway between curve neighbours inside the block; a full block takes a further block from the name's spare; never renumber

checkDigit.binds: name, number and area: the area is the one whose block holds the number, so a check is valid for exactly one area
checkDigit.why: every area of one name shares the prefix, so Damm rejects every single wrong digit and every neighbour swap, including typos that land in another same-named area (582,688 sampled on the plate-name register, 0 accepted); writing the area id into the check would accept 61,619 of them
checkDigit.printed: never: for systems only (machine records and the API)

referenceTowns.rule: fixed points, never moved, only added; a spot code is shortened (first 4 characters dropped) against the nearest town within 0.4° on both axes; recovery exact within 0.5°
referenceTowns.coverage: the 31 towns reach every building location in Sierra Leone (checked against all Google/Microsoft footprint cells at 0.01°)

rules.rule: confirmed plot (Add my home, survey plan)
estate / institutional compound (N-Ways compounds): parent of compounds inside
dense hectare: more than 70 structures per 100 m cell: no grouping (Kroo Bay, Susan's Bay, Mabella, Colbot, hillside settlements)
village yard: where a hectare has ≤ 25 structures, satellite < 30 m² joins the nearest principal ≥ 30 m² (≥ 2×) within 8 m
town proximity: the same within 4 m elsewhere

compounds.mainStructure: largest footprint unless people confirm another
compounds.gate: confirmed gate > mapped gate/entrance within 3 m of the enclosure > where the nearest road or footpath meets the enclosure > main structure centroid
compounds.regrouping: never changes an issued code (merge keeps the gate compound's code, others become aliases; split keeps it on the part with the original gate)
compounds.wallShops: a shop in the front wall with its own street door is its own structure with its own entrance

inference.signal: one N-Ways place inside the footprint

steps: stand at the gate: GPS averaged ≥ 10 s + one gate photo (its Plus Code is shown at once)

outline: tap corners | walk the boundary with ARKit/ARCore anchored by averaged GPS | import survey-plan beacons (Sierra Leone 1968 / UTM 28N EPSG:2161 or 29N EPSG:2162, 1924 War Office grid, or WGS 84 — chosen, never assumed)
provisional code at once: next free number in the area
confirmed by arrivals/deliveries at the gate, new imagery/footprints, or 30 days without dispute
checks: a point within 3 m of an issued compound, or an outline overlapping more than half of one, gets that compound's code: nothing new is issued
in dense hectares: single structures unless walled
addMyHome.statement: A code is an address, not a land title or survey plan. Land matters go to the Ministry of Lands, Housing and Country Planning / National Land Commission.
addMyHome.offline: Plus Code at once; compound code on next connection

getting.app: shown as "Your home code" (FCC Plus Code in Freetown, N-Ways code elsewhere) as soon as home is known (saved home, or a tap on This is my home at the gate); one tap to share by WhatsApp or SMS link
getting.plates: the plate name and the number in groups, and the gate's Plus Code; in Freetown, FCC's Plus Code first
getting.partners: couriers, banks, utilities, FCC look codes up by location (API)
getting.laterOption: an SMS lookup service (not planned now)

spoken.digits: said digit by digit or in pairs in Krio/English (482 = "fo-et-tu"; 27 16 = "twenti-sevin, sikstin" or "tu-sevin, wan-siks"); Mende and Temne speakers commonly use Krio/English numerals for phone numbers — to field-test

plusCodeLetters.note: Krio letter names follow English; to field-test

sources.buildings: OSM (ODbL); Google Open Buildings (CC BY 4.0); Microsoft (ODbL)
sources.chiefdoms: geoBoundaries SLE ADM3 (CC BY 4.0), statistics only
